verdict.rationale: cubic's core function is generating AI insights and suggestions from the user's own code. It does this through automatic PR reviews that flag bugs and improvements, interactive Q&A in PR comments, an AI chat that reads the PR and codebase, AI wikis with architecture diagrams, and codebase scans. One community user says it gives more technical explanations than general-purpose models. Missing for 10: the analytics dashboards show metrics with no documented AI-generated insights, the AI chat sidebar docs sit under an 'archive' path so its current status is unclear, and there is little independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can get AI-generated insights and suggestions from my data inside the product

citations.quote: Comments on bugs and improvements in pull requests
AI chat answers questions about a pull request while you read it. It reads the PR and the rest of your codebase.
cubic's AI wiki automatically indexes your codebase and produces searchable wikis, complete with links to source code, architecture diagrams, and more.
The AI automatically scans every pull request for a wide range of issues, including logic errors, style inconsistencies, and potential security vulnerabilities.
